summary.intent: The user wanted to understand why the PR's line additions had grown from ~100 to ~400 since the first commit after a fix verification, and reduce the diff size.
summary.outcome: Identified that most growth was in test code (13 new tests across 4 commits). Consolidated redundant tests and trimmed verbose doc comments, reducing the PR from 484 to 387 insertions (net -96 lines) committed as a76bd5b04.

repo: The CLI uses a worktree-based workflow at .worktrees/explain-fix for feature branches
The project uses mise for task running (mise run check) combining fmt, lint, and tests
The explain command grew through 4 additive commits from AI tools (Cursor Bugbot, Codex) that each added tests without consolidating existing ones

code.finding: Three trailer-less tests were near-identical and mergeable into one table-driven test; two sentinel tests were also mergeable. TestRunExplainAuto_NoMatch duplicated coverage already in ChecksPositionalCheckpointIDFirst. TestRunExplainCheckpoint_NotFoundMessageNotDuplicated tested a trivial one-line fmt change not worth a dedicated test.
runExplainAuto and the ambiguity guard had verbose doc comments that added ~15 lines with minimal informational value and were trimmed.

workflow: AI-assisted commits (Bugbot, Codex) tend to append tests without reviewing for overlap with existing coverage, requiring periodic consolidation passes
Separating growth analysis by production vs test lines is a useful diagnostic: here prod was +203/-34 vs tests +281/-24, pointing to test verbosity as the primary driver
Table-driven tests in Go are consistently more line-efficient than individual test functions for near-identical scenarios

friction: Growth accumulated silently across 4 AI-generated commits before the user noticed, suggesting lack of per-commit diff size awareness
Redundant tests introduced by different AI tools (Cursor, Codex) required manual deduplication analysis
open_items: PR still at 387 insertions — further reduction may be possible if the feature itself can be simplified, but was not pursued
No mechanism in place to prevent future AI-assisted commits from reintroducing redundant tests
